m.s: Score the skin of {duck} in a crisscross, cutting into the fat but not the meat. Rub all over with {fivespice} and salt. Leave for 20 minutes.

Rinse {rice} until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1½ times its volume of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes so it finishes steaming.

Place the duck skin side down in a cold frying pan, then turn the heat to medium. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, pouring off the fat into a bowl as it renders, until the skin is deep golden and crisp. Starting cold is the trick: it melts the fat before the skin burns.
Flip and cook for 3 to 4 minutes for pink in the middle. Rest on a board for 8 minutes.

Wipe the pan, then add {soy}, {honey} and grated {ginger} and bubble for 1 minute until syrupy. In another pan, stir-fry {bokchoy}, halved, with crushed {garlic} in a spoonful of the duck fat for 2 minutes.
Slice the duck, spoon over the glaze and serve with the rice, bok choy, sliced {springonion} and {sesameseeds}.

l: Slice the duck thin over rice and greens. Good cold or barely warm. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: Tamari instead of soy for the GF glaze, made in a separate pan. Check the five spice.
